title: Microsoft Dataverse: Python SDK for scripting and agent workflows
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, licensing statements and governance calls are supported by the sources checked. The application-user UI path stops before the security-role selector, a minor omission; its note already describes that remaining step.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Scope; rationale: risk
claims.claim: SDK data operations enforce existing Dataverse security roles rather than a separate permission model.
claims.quote: Role-based access control: Enforces Dataverse security roles and policies for all data operations.

claims.claim: Table or column metadata changes require privileges to customize the table.
claims.quote: Creating a column is a metadata change: you need privileges to customize the table

claims.claim: SDK users can extract Dataverse tables into pandas DataFrames for analysis.
claims.quote: Extract and transform: Load tables into Pandas DataFrames for cleaning, feature engineering, and exploratory analysis.

claims.claim: Extracted data outside Dataverse is no longer protected by the Dataverse security boundary.
claims.quote: after the data has been extracted it is no longer protected by the security boundary provided by Dynamics 365 (online) and is instead controlled directly by the customer.

claims.quote:

credential = InteractiveBrowserCredential()  # Browser authentication

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: The SDK's authentication identity depends on the Azure Identity credential supplied.
claims.quote: The SDK client requires any Azure Identity TokenCredential implementation for OAuth authentication with Dataverse.

claims.claim: InteractiveBrowserCredential accepts a client_id identifying the application users sign into.
claims.quote: Client ID of the Microsoft Entra application that users will sign into.

claims.claim: Without client_id, InteractiveBrowserCredential authenticates to an Azure development application.
claims.quote: If not specified, users will authenticate to an Azure development application, which is not recommended for production scenarios.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: client.files.upload automatically creates a missing file column.
claims.quote: If the file column doesn't exist, the SDK creates it automatically.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Automatically creating a file column permanently changes the environment schema.
claims.quote: the new column becomes a permanent part of your environment's schema.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Learn advises creating file columns in advance in production.
claims.quote: In production environments, create file columns in advance rather than relying on automatic creation.

claims.claim: dataverse-install-claude-skill optionally installs Claude skills after the package installation.
claims.quote: pip install PowerPlatform-Dataverse-Client && dataverse-install-claude-skill

claims.claim: That optional installation installs two Claude skills.
claims.quote: you can optionally install two Claude Skills when installing the SDK from a package.

claims.claim: The installed skill definitions reside on the developer's computer.
claims.quote: you can find skill definitions in the .claude/skills/dataverse-sdk-use/SKILL.md and .claude/skills/dataverse-sdk-dev/SKILL.md files on your development computer.

claims.claim: The SDK automatically retries temporary failures such as throttling.
claims.quote: Handle networking problems that might occur for operations that fail due to temporary problems, such as API throttling or service unavailability.

claims.claim: Dataverse service protection limits apply to external web service requests, including SDK traffic.
claims.quote: Service protection limits apply to all external web service requests, not only the CRUD operations on tables counted against entitlement limits.

claims.claim: Shared user-account service protection limits mean heavy scripts can affect other callers using that account.
claims.quote: We limit the number of concurrent connections per user account, the number of API requests per connection, and the amount of execution time that can be used for each connection.

claims.claim: Dataverse CRUD, assign and share operations count toward Power Platform request limits.
claims.quote: Dataverse: All create, read, update, and delete (CRUD), assign, and share operations including user-driven and internal system requests required to complete CRUD transactions, and special operations like share or assign.

claims.claim: Those request limits cover any client or application and SOAP or REST endpoints, so SDK data traffic counts.
claims.quote: These operations can be from any client or application (including Dynamics 365) and use any endpoint (SOAP or REST).

claims.claim: Application, non-interactive, administrative and system users share tenant-level request limits.
claims.quote: All application users, non-interactive users, administrative users, and system users within the tenant share tenant-level limits.

claims.claim: Writing rows and files consumes Dataverse storage capacity.
claims.quote: All Dataverse tables, including system tables, are included in the storage capacity reports. Files such as .pdf (or any other file attachment type) are stored in file storage.
